owned_objects_bytes.scope: All driver objects are disjoint static storage. Live prediction and prospective correction occupy the existing live state/candidate pair. Candidate also stages checkpoint restore; no third state, scratch full matrix, new vector or whole-record serialization buffer. Query storage is counted simultaneously.
owned_objects_bytes.trajectory_dependence: Fixed dimensions, no inference heap, raw journal, age-growing cached rows or history-length loop. The lower factor uses the existing full 16x16 array; packing its unused upper entries is not part of this experiment.

readonly_configuration.host_placement: nm reports lower and upper in read-only storage. The checkpoint magic may be folded into compiler constants; do not add its logical 8 B again to measured .rodata.
readonly_configuration.other_constants: Math constants, status/format strings, code and host link tables are additional; whole-host ELF section inventory is separate.
readonly_configuration.target_rule: Readonly arrays require explicit flash/SRAM placement in a target linker map. If both support arrays are copied into SRAM, add 256 B to the owned RAM subtotal. Custom OCV tables would be additional; this candidate uses the built-in illustrative OCV with no backing table.

stack.interpretation: Conservative source call-chain sums retain small helper/tail frames that may be inlined or eliminated; inlined locals are already in callers. The 2328 B alternative sums mutually exclusive own function frames and the reached OCV frame; it is deliberately loose, not a simultaneous measured peak. No own-source recursion or variable-length automatic array.
stack.exclusions: Libm/libc/formatting/parsing/syscall-wrapper stack, external callers, startup, interrupts and target compiler/ABI effects. No complete machine call-graph or runtime worst-case stack proof.

partial_subtotals_bytes.notes: Alternative scopes, not addends. Named objects are globals, so adding own-source frames does not double count them. Remaining link sections, shared-library/runtime stack and allocations, acquisition/interrupt/persistence/target requirements remain additional. No subtotal qualifies a complete 10240 B subsystem.

persistence.identity: SCMONLN2 / A4SREKF2; version 1 rejected without conversion.
persistence.restore_candidate: Existing 2424 B workspace.candidate receives prospective decoded state, already included in 2936 B workspace. Destination replacement follows complete validation.
persistence.stdio_buffer: Reuse existing 128 B observation_gradient vector for save/restore. Persistence cannot overlap ingestion/correction with the same workspace.
persistence.temporary_filename_scope: Already inside the compiler-reported 656 B save frame; do not add again.
persistence.field_codec_buffers: Fixed 4/8 B codec locals are inside reported helper/caller frames. The 256 B restore frame includes codec/stat locals; no entire payload is staged on stack.
persistence.external_storage_scope: Current and temporary records may coexist during replacement: 2x2456 B of persistent record data, plus filesystem metadata or deliberately retained archives. This is not SRAM.
persistence.unqualified: FILE objects, fopen/fdopen/mkstemp/stdio internals, filesystem cache and full library stack remain additional. Directory power-loss durability, MCU flash staging/erase/program protocol and wear are outside host codec qualification.

host_executable.bss_difference: 96 B comprises 17 B of named stdout/stderr/runtime flags plus 79 B of layout/alignment. Separate .data is 16 B of host runtime data; other dynamic/link sections and shared libraries also consume memory.
host_executable.scope: Whole host executable includes CSV/JSON/persistence plumbing and the shared model object. File/text/read-only sizes are not M23 flash forecasts or complete resident-memory measurements.

retained_history_M1.scope: Observed requested session-plus-fit ownership, not total process RSS or complete stack. Most storage is 640 B of cached design rows per sample, allowing historical nonlinear reevaluation; the belief mean itself is small. New online memory savings exchange exact retained-history access for a local sequential Gaussian approximation.

earlier_fixed_chart_compact.scope: Fixed-chart evidence/remainder subsystem with a different ownership and inference contract; not an autonomous broad-prior nonlinear learner and not complete firmware. It preserves conditional information within a declared chart rather than retaining raw nonlinear history. Do not infer equivalent accuracy, uncertainty guarantees or functionality from the similar byte count.

comparisons.new_candidate: 002 owns 5896 B core and 7064 B named host objects, including autonomous component-gain learning, full state/parameter correlation and complete fixed persistence. Its estimation quality and qualification are decided separately by the first frozen falsification; memory eligibility is insufficient.
comparisons.same_number_note: The new 7064 B named host subtotal happens to equal the older fixed-chart 7064 B subsystem total. Different objects, inference semantics and recovery functionality make this numerical equality incidental.

fixed_work.prediction: Same sparse F*L on five physical-state rows; source loops visit 16 entries per changed row. Static rows and full correlations are carried. No historical nonlinear relinearization.
fixed_work.rotation_scope: First pass forms the optimal local factor and normalized gain; second appends d=g-t and restores a lower factor for the actual component gain. Second-pass identity rotations skip. No general dense QR, inverse, rank threshold or covariance floor.
fixed_work.state_copies: Source has three fixed 2424 B state assignments on a successful voltage step: into candidate, prediction commit, correction commit. Missing voltage or rejected correction uses two. This is copied-byte work, not extra simultaneously owned RAM; compiler implementation may differ.
fixed_work.zero_gain_work: All-zero selected gain additionally restores 128 B mean and 2048 B factor from committed prediction for exact bytes; the factor round-trip is not used as a numerical no-op.
fixed_work.query: Fixed 16 row norms over 16 entries, scalar target transforms and status checks.
fixed_work.persistence: Fixed 2456 B canonical record and bounded codec loops; filesystem latency is not bounded by source loop lengths.
fixed_work.scope: Fixed source work independent of trajectory age. No M23 cycle, worst-case execution time, throughput or energy measurement.

comparison_to_001.fixed_storage_reason: The new 16 B of maximum-scale/mask diagnostics occurs in state, candidate and query; only one state copy is serialized. Factor and vector allocation sizes are unchanged.
comparison_to_001.stack_layout_reason: Compiler code generation changes the ingest frame; this is a host measurement, not an equivalent M23 improvement. ELF alignment absorbs 32 B of the 48 B named-object increase, so .bss grows 16 B.
comparison_to_001.work_change: 001 uses two dense matrix-vector products and a scalar-lambda factor correction. 002 uses one triangular gradient product and two triangular orthogonal passes for the actual component gain. Both are fixed O(16 squared); operation structure and state-copy counts differ, so no speedup is inferred from asymptotic order.
comparison_to_001.quality_separation: Resource comparisons do not establish that 002 fixes capacity bias or local overconfidence. Its first frozen scoring/qualification result is separate.
